text:
South Boston never forgets. Hundreds of our friends and neighbors came together to celebrate Mass at St. Brigid Church, mark the 45th anniversary of the dedication of the South Boston Vietnam Veterans Memorial, and honor the 25 service members from our neighborhood who were killed in Vietnam.

The South Boston Vietnam Veterans Memorial was among the first memorials constructed in our County honoring Vietnam veterans in 1981, when opposition over the war’s aims and human costs made such memorials controversial. At that time, a small group of veterans led by Tom Lyons persevered in establishing a suitable memorial to ensure that the courage and sacrifice of 25 young men from South Boston would be remembered.

Thank you to former U.S. Senator Jim Webb, our guest speaker, for your inspiring words and your dedication to public service to our nation. Thank you also to Vocalist John McDermott and to Tommy Lyons for your relentless advocacy on behalf of your fellow veterans and for organizing such a meaningful event.

It was great to be joined by so many Gold Star families as well as my colleagues in government, Mayor Wu, @nickcollinsma, @SCDAONews, @EdforBoston, @ErinforBoston, and Clerk of Courts John Powers.

text:
ROAD TO 250: Long Island and Queens Legacies

One of George Washington’s most important spies lived right here on Long Island — and for generations, almost no one knew it.

Robert Townsend of Oyster Bay was “Culper Junior,” a key member of Washington’s Culper Spy Ring. From British-occupied New York City, he secretly gathered intelligence and passed it back to Washington.

His family home, Raynham Hall, still stands in #NY03.

As we continue to celebrate America’s 250th, I’m proud to highlight this remarkable piece of our local history. I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to establish the Washington Spy Ring National Historic Trail and help preserve the story of Townsend and the Culper spies for generations to come.

ROAD TO 250: Our Local American Stories

As we continue to celebrate America’s 250th, here’s a story from our own backyard.

Robert Townsend of Oyster Bay was “Culper Junior,” one of George Washington’s most important spies. From British-occupied New York City, he secretly gathered intelligence for the American cause.

His family home, @RaynhamHall still stands in Oyster Bay today.

Nearly 250 years later, Townsend’s story reminds us just how much of America’s history was made right here on Long Island.

text:
I have said from the start that the map drawn in a back room in Jeff City, for the sole purpose of handing Donald Trump a seat he could not win, was unconstitutional. 

More than 300,000 Missourians signed their names to say the same thing.

The courts have now agreed. Missouri will vote in November under the lines that were lawfully in place, and Missourians get the final say on whether that back room map ever takes effect at all. I am asking every voter in this state to reject it.

Understand what the gerrymandered map was built to do. They drew it to erase Rep. Emanuel Cleaver, an institution and a mentor, a man who has represented Kansas City for two decades, because they could not beat him at the ballot box. 

It carved roughly 70,000 minority residents out of his district and used Troost Avenue, a street that has stood for segregation in Kansas City for a century, as the dividing line. In my district, it also watered down the voice of the St. Louisans who live here.

I spent years as a prosecutor. I know what it looks like when someone decides the law applies to everyone but them. They may have given it everything they had, but Missourians refused to let it stand.

Voters pick their representatives. Not the other way around. Anyone who wants to serve the public would be wise to remember that.

text:
The lesson is clear.

The Trump Administration was naive to believe in Big Tech's willingness to restrain itself, just as Big Tech is naive to think its abrupt remorse excuses years of negligence and recklessness. The “fail fast” mindset might work fine in Silicon Valley, but it falls to pieces when our civil rights, safety online, and cybersecurity are abandoned in the name of giving these companies more personal data to use and abuse.

I have continuously called for stronger standards on impact assessments, pre-deployment testing, and algorithmic accountability and transparency. I would be more than happy to deliver those demands directly to the billionaires who put us in this terribly dangerous position if Speaker Johnson bothers to let Democrats in the room with them.

text: RT @BarackObama: I was encouraged this week to see the leaders of the frontier labs agree on the need for them to slow down the pace of AI…

reposted.text:
I was encouraged this week to see the leaders of the frontier labs agree on the need for them to slow down the pace of AI development. Given the stakes, it’s a good and necessary first step.
 
But I’m even more encouraged by the growing recognition that how this powerful new technology develops should be at the center of our public debate.
 
I’ve been watching the progress on AI for over a decade now, and one thing that’s clear to me is that the potential impact of this technology is not overhyped. It’s also moving at lightning speed – and even faster than those who are engineering it can keep up with.
 
I’m not an AI accelerationist who believes it will lead to some techno-utopia, and I’m not a doomer who thinks it will inevitably lead to humanity’s destruction.

But whether this technology results in amazing breakthroughs in medicine, energy and education or unleashes huge economic disruptions, greater inequality, and potential catastrophe will depend on the choices that we make right now – choices that should be made not just by the companies involved, but by all of us.

Our families deserve a government that focuses on what matters, works across party lines, and delivers results. I’ll keep showing up, working hard, and fighting for the communities we call home. 

Glad to champion the following bills:

▪️ H.R. 309, National Law Enforcement Officers Remembrance, Support and Community Outreach Act, would support community outreach, public safety education, and officer wellness initiatives. Our law enforcement officers put themselves on the line for us, and we have a responsibility to stand behind them.

▪️ H.R. 979, AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, would preserve access to AM radio in new vehicles. When hurricanes and severe storms knock out power or cell service, eastern North Carolinians need reliable access to emergency information.

▪️ H.R. 1266, Combating Illicit Xylazine Act, would strengthen law enforcement tools to combat the illicit use and trafficking of xylazine while preserving legitimate veterinary uses. We must keep dangerous drugs off our streets while protecting the farmers and veterinarians who rely on xylazine for legitimate purposes.

quoted.text:
BREAKING: The Supreme Court has DENIED the Trump regime's emergency request to enforce new mail-ballot restrictions ahead of the midterm elections.

The ruling leaves in place a preliminary injunction blocking the U.S. Postal Service from requiring states to submit voter information through a federal portal, obtain approval for ballot-envelope designs, and comply with new barcode requirements.

Justice Kavanaugh joined the denial, writing that imposing the rule so close to the election would likely be “arbitrary and capricious” because state and local officials lack sufficient time to implement it.

Justices Alito and Thomas dissented. The underlying litigation will continue, but the restrictions remain blocked for the 2026 midterms.
